events.headline: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel Death Toll Rises to 6 in Mexico, 10+ Missing in Baja California
events.summary: As of Oct 13, 2026, the combined death toll from Hurricane Simon and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel reached 6 in Mexico. A 71-year-old man died in Guerrero when Simon, which had peaked as a Category 4 storm, caused a retaining wall collapse, while at least 4 people died and 10 or more are missing in Baja California (8 near Ensenada, 2 near San Felipe) after Rachel's remnants hit. New landfalls are forecast for the weekend of Oct 17-18.

events.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Cases Pass 9,000 as Death Toll Tops 4,300, History's Deadliest
events.summary: As of Oct 13, 2026, the DRC's Ebola outbreak has recorded over 9,000 confirmed cases and more than 4,300 deaths, making it history's deadliest Ebola outbreak behind only the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic. The outbreak remains centered in Ituri Province.

events.headline: Houthi Missile Strikes Saudi Aramco Headquarters in Dhahran, Setting Office Tower Ablaze
events.summary: A Houthi missile struck Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex in Dhahran on Oct 13, 2026, damaging the top three floors and sparking a limited fire, with no injuries reported at the site. The strike is part of an intensifying Houthi campaign that has also hit Riyadh and other Saudi cities, killing at least 18-20 people and wounding hundreds over the preceding week.

events.headline: 13 of 17 Sudan Nutrition Surveys Since January Find Critical Malnutrition; 300,000+ Newly Displaced in Kordofan
events.summary: A new famine-risk assessment found that 13 of 17 nutrition surveys conducted in Sudan since January 2026 recorded critical acute malnutrition, with Greater Kordofan, the epicenter, seeing more than 300,000 people newly displaced since October 2025. A WFP convoy was struck by an airstrike in South Kordofan on Oct 3, killing a driver, a day after another WFP truck hit an explosive device, as the humanitarian response faces severe funding shortfalls.

events.headline: Spain's Sánchez Calls Snap Election After Madrid Eviction Death Protests
events.summary: About 20,000 people marched in Madrid on Oct 8-9 mourning Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old evicted pensioner who died weeks later, after Congress rejected Sánchez's housing-relief decrees on Oct 2. Sánchez subsequently dissolved parliament and called a snap general election for Nov 29, 2026.

events.headline: Russian Strikes Hit Kharkiv Power Plant and Kyiv Energy Facility, Grocery Store Attack Kills 3
events.summary: Russia struck a power plant in Kharkiv and an energy facility in Kyiv hours after Trump's claimed energy ceasefire announcement. A separate strike on a grocery store killed three people and injured 22 others.

events.headline: Kenya Confirms First Imported Ebola Death as DRC Outbreak Toll Hits 4,242
events.summary: Kenya confirmed its first imported Ebola case, a patient who died October 5 in Nairobi, as the Democratic Republic of Congo's outbreak toll climbed to 8,787 cases and 4,242 deaths, the deadliest in history. Kenya has stepped up cross-border screening in response.

events.headline: Eritrean Troops Cross Into Tigray; Ethiopia Says It Regained Border City After Drone Strikes
events.summary: Witnesses reported Eritrean troops crossing into Ethiopia's Tigray region near Zalambessa and Adigrat, prompting Ethiopian drone strikes on the column. Ethiopia says it has since regained control of a border city as rhetoric between the two countries escalates toward war.

events.headline: Blue Nile Drone Strike Death Toll Rises to at Least 72 Sudanese Miners
events.summary: A rights monitor says the death toll from a drone strike on gold miners in Sudan's Blue Nile region has risen to at least 72, up from an earlier count of 41. The strike targeted a displacement camp and mining site in Wad al-Mahi.
events.locationName: Wad al-Mahi, Blue Nile State, Sudan

events.headline: Panama Earthquake Toll Rises: Hotel and Church Collapse in Tonosí, 27+ Injured
events.summary: Aftershocks from Panama's magnitude-7.7 earthquake continue, with a hotel and church collapsing in Tonosí and more than 27 people injured. Nationwide damage now includes over 142 homes and 188 schools, with 147 aftershocks recorded since the quake.

events.headline: Rights Groups Say Gaza Ceasefire 'Exists in Name Only' as Toll Since Truce Tops 1,400
events.summary: More than 100 NGOs say the Gaza ceasefire 'exists in name only,' citing over 1,400 people killed since the truce took effect. Israeli forces reportedly killed six people in Gaza, including a child, in recent strikes.

events.headline: Trump Says Ukraine Needs 'New President' After Diesel-Deal Clash
events.summary: On Oct 10, Trump said Ukraine 'needs a new president,' blaming President Zelenskyy's refinery strikes for rising diesel prices, after Zelenskyy condemned a new US-Russia diesel export deal. The sharp public rupture comes weeks after Trump signed a Russia sanctions law.

events.headline: Pakistan Declares Emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Arrests PTI Chief Minister
events.summary: Pakistan's federal government declared emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province and arrested PTI Chief Minister Sohail Afridi along with seven other party leaders. The crackdown marks a major escalation against Imran Khan's party in the province.

events.headline: Trump-Putin Diesel Deal Waives Russia Sanctions Through April 2027
events.summary: Putin agreed on Oct 9 to supply global diesel markets, including up to 3 million tons of exports, to help lower US fuel prices ahead of the midterms, and the US Treasury issued a temporary license permitting sale, delivery and import of Russian diesel through April 7, 2027. Senate Democrats and Zelenskyy criticized the arrangement.

events.headline: Russian Missiles Strike Kyiv's CHP-4 Power Plant and Apartment Building, Killing 2, Injuring 21
events.summary: On the night of Oct 13, 2026, Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv's CHPP-4 power plant in the Darnytsia district and a nine-story residential building in Desnianskyi district, killing at least 2 people and injuring 21. President Zelensky said Western partners gave no advance warning for a second consecutive night, days after a Trump-announced energy ceasefire.

events.headline: Drone Strikes Sink Cargo Ship Off Bulgaria's Black Sea Coast, 11 Sailors Missing
events.summary: Overnight Oct 12-13, 2026, drones struck two cargo ships in Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone; a Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel sank off Krapets with 11 of 16 crew still missing, while a Malta-flagged ship's 15 crew were rescued safely. Bulgaria summoned Russia's ambassador and requested NATO/EU assistance, with its president saying the outcome benefits Russia.

events.headline: Former DRC President Kabila Forms New Rebel Group Aligned With M23 in Goma
events.summary: Former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila has formed the 'Front for the Refoundation of the Nation,' aligning openly with the M23/AFC insurgency in Goma. The move marks Kabila's formal emergence as a rebel leader against the Congolese government.

events.headline: Trump Says Iran Decision Coming 'Very Soon' as Houthi Attacks and Hormuz Tensions Escalate
events.summary: On Oct 13, 2026, President Trump told reporters he would decide on Iran 'very soon' amid renewed attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, adding that the Nov 3 midterm elections have 'no impact' on the timing. A White House official denied Trump had discussed resuming military action with Netanyahu and reiterated there would be no US strike before the midterms.

events.headline: China Holds Five-Day Military Drills Across Four Seas as Taiwan Unveils $850M Ammo Stockpile Plan
events.summary: China conducted five days of live-fire drills spanning the Bohai, Yellow, East China and South China seas, prompting condemnation from Taiwan. Taiwan's defense ministry separately announced an NT$27 billion ($850 million), six-year plan to quadruple its ammunition stockpile from 30 to 120 days amid continued Chinese military pressure.

events.headline: Kospi Closes Below 6,100 as Samsung, SK Hynix Plunge Further on Chinese Rival CXMT Fears
events.summary: South Korea's Kospi index closed down 5.46% at 6,035.35 on Oct 13, 2026, with an intraday low of 5,911, its first drop below 6,000 since late July. Samsung Electronics fell 7.4% and SK Hynix fell 10.1%, driven by concerns over Chinese memory maker CXMT's new high-density memory-cell design and roughly $3.4 billion in net foreign outflows that day.

events.headline: Post-Tropical Isaías Kills Four, Triggers Flooding and Tornadoes Across Southeast US
events.summary: After making landfall near Destin, Florida as a Category 2 hurricane, Isaías weakened to a post-tropical storm but killed at least four people and spawned flooding and tornadoes across the southeastern United States.

events.headline: US Sanctions Cartel del Noreste Business Network; Mexico Seizes 48 Drones, Explosives in Sinaloa
events.summary: On Oct 13, 2026, US Treasury's OFAC sanctioned four individuals and 11 entities tied to Cartel del Noreste's business network centered on Nuevo Laredo, spanning horse racing, construction, trucking and energy firms. Separately, Mexico's security forces reported seizing 48 drones, explosive devices, landmines and a dismantled drug lab across Culiacán, Mazatlán and nearby Sinaloa municipalities between Oct 9-12.

events.headline: Zamfara Bandits Ambush Military-Escorted Traders, Killing About 20; Villages Torched in Maru
events.summary: On Oct 11-12, 2026, bandits ambushed traders traveling under military escort along the Gwashi-Nasarawa road in Bukkuyum LGA, killing approximately 20-22 soldiers, police and civilians. Separately, bandits torched about 12 vehicles and displaced over 300 residents from three villages along the Dansadau road in Maru LGA, Zamfara State.

events.headline: Debris From Intercepted Houthi Missiles Injures Four, Damages 15 Homes in Riyadh
events.summary: Saudi Civil Defense said debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles injured four people, including a woman and a child, and damaged 15 homes in Riyadh on Oct 13, 2026. The coalition separately intercepted two more ballistic missiles as part of a broader campaign that closed Riyadh's airport and has killed 18-20 people over the preceding week.

events.headline: Alberta Independence Vote Nears as Support for Secession Holds Near 22%
events.summary: Ahead of Alberta's October 19 independence referendum, polling shows only about 22% support for separation from Canada. Prime Minister Carney has issued Brexit-style warnings about the economic risks of secession.

events.headline: UN Allocates $75M for Haiti as Drone Attack Deaths Surge 120%, Topping 1,200 Civilians Killed in 2026
events.summary: The UN allocated an additional $75 million for Haiti on Oct 12, 2026, funding 10 projects across Ouest, Centre and Artibonite departments to reach over 500,000 people. Drone attacks have surged 120% this year, killing more than 1,200 civilians including 17 children; over 6 million people need assistance and 1.5 million are displaced, while the Humanitarian Response Plan remains less than half funded.

events.headline: US Measles Cases Top 4,080, Elimination Status at Risk; Florida Dengue Outbreak Largest in Decades
events.summary: US measles cases have climbed past 4,080, with health officials warning the country is highly likely to lose its measles elimination status this fall. Separately, Florida is experiencing its largest dengue outbreak in decades with roughly 300 cases.

events.headline: China's September Exports Surge 36%, Nine-Month Trade Surplus Nears $938 Billion
events.summary: China's exports rose 36.3% year-on-year in September 2026, the fastest pace since February, reaching a record $447.18 billion, while imports grew 31%. The monthly trade surplus of $133.5 billion was a 20-month high, bringing the nine-month cumulative surplus to roughly $938 billion, driven by semiconductor exports up 108% and auto exports up 54% year-on-year.

events.headline: Thousands Protest Contaminated Water in Guadalajara, Dozens Arrested
events.summary: Around 10,000 people marched in Guadalajara, Mexico over contaminated water supplies, resulting in clashes that injured 28 police officers and 31 civilians. Authorities arrested 39 people as President Sheinbaum faced demands for answers.

events.headline: Taliban Rejects Pakistani Accusations of Harboring TTP Militants Amid Kurram Border Tensions
events.summary: Following a deadly clash in Pakistan's Kurram District, Islamabad urged the Afghan Taliban government to stop cross-border attacks by the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid rejected the accusations, saying there are 'no TTP bases in Afghanistan' and accusing Pakistan of prioritizing propaganda over dialogue.

events.headline: Airstrike on Sudan-Egypt Border Gold-Mining Sites Kills at Least 72, Investigation Launched
events.summary: An airstrike on gold-mining sites near the Sudan-Egypt border in Red Sea state killed at least 72 people, according to a rights monitor, prompting an investigation. Egypt has acknowledged conducting a 'third phase' anti-mining operation near the border but has not confirmed casualty figures.

events.headline: France Opens 2027 Budget Debate Targeting 5.0% Deficit as Debt Hits 119% of GDP
events.summary: France's National Assembly opened debate on the 2027 budget on Oct 13, 2026, targeting a deficit of 5.0% of GDP, down from 5.4%, through roughly 54 billion euros in savings and revenue measures. Public debt has climbed to 3.6 trillion euros, or 119% of GDP, the highest since 1946, with debt projected to reach 121.7% in 2027.

events.headline: EU Formally Adopts Record 1,646-Entry Russia Sanctions List
events.summary: The EU's Foreign Affairs Council formally adopted its largest-ever Russia sanctions expansion on October 12, listing 1,646 individuals and entities tied to drone and missile production. The package had been agreed by ambassadors earlier in the week.

events.headline: North Korea Fires Two Ballistic Missiles Into Sea of Japan
events.summary: North Korea launched two ballistic missiles, traveling roughly 220km and 910km, into the Sea of Japan, in apparent response to a South Korean hypersonic missile test.

events.headline: Brazil Heads to Oct 25 Runoff: Flávio Bolsonaro Narrowly Leads Lula
events.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro won 47% of the first-round vote to Lula's 45%, setting up a tight runoff election on October 25. Polling shows the race remains close as Brazil's electorate stays deeply polarized.

events.headline: Saudi-Led Coalition Strikes Houthi Oil and Military Sites in Sanaa, Dhamar and Saada
events.summary: In retaliation for Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, a Saudi-led coalition struck oil facilities including the Yemen Petroleum Company and military sites in Dhamar and Saada on Oct 13, 2026. An evacuation order was issued in Sanaa before the strikes, and Houthi television reported civilian casualties.

events.headline: Canada Sheds 68,000 Jobs in September, Unemployment Climbs to 6.5%
events.summary: Statistics Canada reported a loss of roughly 68,000 jobs in September 2026, far exceeding expectations of a 9,000 gain and following a loss of about 42,000 in August. Unemployment rose to 6.5% from 6.4%, with youth employment (ages 15-24) down 48,000 and labor force participation at its lowest non-pandemic level in 29 years; the Bank of Canada's next rate decision is Oct 28.

events.headline: Bank of America Fined $1.21 Billion for Anti-Money-Laundering and Sanctions Violations
events.summary: On Oct 13, 2026, the US Treasury imposed a combined $1.21 billion penalty on Bank of America, with FinCEN assessing $1.2B and OCC levying a record $750M for failing to report over $5 billion in suspicious transactions linked to Chinese laundering networks and border illicit finance. OFAC separately settled for $11.6M over sanctions violations involving Iran, Russia and narcotics programs. The bank admitted willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act, making this the third-largest Treasury penalty in history.

events.headline: IMF Cuts Argentina's 2026 Growth Forecast to 2.1% as Milei Begins Washington Visit
events.summary: The IMF's October World Economic Outlook cut Argentina's 2026 growth forecast to 2.1% from 3.5%, citing weak third-quarter activity, while raising inflation projections to 32.5% and unemployment to 7.6%. President Javier Milei began a two-day visit to Washington on Oct 14 to reinforce ties with the Trump administration and address the US Chamber of Commerce.

events.headline: Myanmar Deepens Nationwide Power Rationing as Heatwave Strains Grid
events.summary: Myanmar's junta has intensified electricity rationing nationwide, with some areas like Ayeyarwady receiving as little as two hours of power out of every eight, as an El Niño-driven heatwave strains the national grid already weakened by conflict.

events.headline: Singapore's Haze Hits 2026-Season Worst as Indonesian Fires Persist
events.summary: Singapore's air quality index reached 181, its worst level of the 2026 haze season, as fires in Indonesia continue to blanket the region in smoke. Malaysia and Indonesia are coordinating a diplomatic response as millions of students remain affected by school closures.

events.headline: Colombia's Peace Tribunal Charges 10 Former FARC Commanders With War Crimes
events.summary: Colombia's JEP transitional justice tribunal charged 10 former FARC commanders, including ex-senator Julián Gallo, with 44 acts of violence committed between 1996 and 2016 against the Nukak Baka, Korebaju, Siona, Hitnu and Jiw Indigenous peoples in the Amazon-Orinoquia region. The accused have 30 days to respond to the charges.

events.headline: Bangladesh's 2026 Measles Outbreak Death Toll Reaches 1,155
events.summary: As of Oct 10, 2026, Bangladesh's nationwide measles outbreak, which began March 15, 2026, has caused 1,155 deaths (104 confirmed, 1,051 suspected) out of 205,028 total suspected cases and 22,421 confirmed cases. The outbreak continues nationwide amid strained health resources.

events.headline: Fighting Intensifies in Donetsk as Ukraine Reports 264 Clashes in 24 Hours
events.summary: Heavy fighting continues around Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka in Ukraine's Donetsk region, with Ukrainian forces reporting 264 clashes with Russian troops in a single 24-hour period. Civilian and military casualties are rising in the contested area.

events.headline: Nigerian Air Force Plane Crash Death Toll Revised to 25 in Ondo State
events.summary: Nigeria's military revised the death toll from an Air Force ATR-42 crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, to 25 people, down from an earlier reported 32 aboard. The government declared three days of national mourning.

events.headline: Delhi Police File FIRs Against Rahul Gandhi, Kharge Over INDIA Bloc's March to Supreme Court
events.summary: Following an Oct 12, 2026 march by INDIA-bloc leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Priyanka Gandhi toward the Supreme Court to protest the Election Commission's voter-roll revision, Delhi Police registered at least two FIRs for alleged breach of prohibitory orders and barricade-breaking. Eleven opposition leaders separately filed a joint Supreme Court petition challenging the revision exercise.

events.headline: Two Killed During Olive Harvest in South Lebanon Amid Israeli Shelling
events.summary: Two people were killed while harvesting olives in south Lebanon's Yater and Froun areas near Bint Jbeil, reportedly from Israeli shelling or unexploded ordnance. The deaths occurred near the Israel-Lebanon border area where tensions remain elevated.

events.headline: US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle Resigns Amid Misconduct Allegations
events.summary: Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned as US ambassador to Greece on Oct 13, 2026, after the White House requested her resignation following a Wall Street Journal report alleging she solicited $100,000 from a donor, threatened a host-country official, and accepted improper gifts. Guilfoyle denies the allegations.

events.headline: Takaichi's Food Consumption-Tax Cut Advances in Diet as Farm Minister Scandal Overshadows Agenda
events.summary: Japan's cabinet submitted legislation on Oct 9, 2026, to cut the consumption tax on food from 8% to 1% for two years starting April 2027, alongside low-income cash support. The plan has been overshadowed by Agriculture Minister Kazuo Yana facing election-law-violation allegations after boasting he cut road funding to municipalities backing his rival; PM Takaichi reprimanded him but kept him in office.

events.headline: Fire Destroys Paris's Oldest Covered Market, Marché des Enfants Rouges
events.summary: A large fire destroyed the Marché des Enfants Rouges, Paris's oldest covered food market, dating to the 17th century. No injuries were reported but the historic structure was severely damaged.

events.headline: Toxic Algal Bloom Closes Beaches Near Townsville, Australia, Causing Fish Die-Off
events.summary: A Trichodesmium algal bloom has closed swimming sites near Magnetic Island and Townsville, Australia, causing a fish die-off that has persisted since June and was recently extended by wind patterns.

events.headline: Egypt's Foreign Reserves Hit Record $57.35 Billion as UAE Renews Currency Swap
events.summary: Egypt's net international reserves rose to a record $57.35 billion in September, bolstered by a renewed five-year, AED 5 billion currency swap agreement with the UAE.

events.headline: Thai PM Anutin Calls Opposition's Censure Motion Wording 'Hazy,' Delaying Formal Notification
events.summary: After an Oct 8, 2026 no-confidence motion was filed against Prime Minister Anutin and 17 ministers, Anutin publicly criticized the motion's wording as unclear. He suggested this ambiguity is why the House Speaker had not formally notified the government of the censure motion as of Oct 13.

events.headline: Germany Doubles 2026 Growth Forecast to 1.3% on Manufacturing Rebound
events.summary: Germany's government raised its 2026 economic growth forecast from 0.5% to 1.3%, citing an unexpected rally in manufacturing output. The upgrade marks a notable improvement in Europe's largest economy.

events.headline: Foot-and-Mouth Disease Spreads to Second Namibian Region as EU Suspends Meat Imports
events.summary: Namibia has confirmed 127 foot-and-mouth disease cases across 15 farms, with the outbreak first declared in the //Kharas region in late September and spreading to the Zambezi Region by Oct 7, 2026. The EU suspended imports of fresh Namibian beef, sheep and goat meat, removing the market that received 80.7% of Namibia's 2025 beef exports.

events.headline: Kenya's Ruto Calls Kenyatta a 'Conman' as 2027 Succession Battle Escalates
events.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto publicly called former President Uhuru Kenyatta a 'conman,' accusing him of breaking an informal succession pact, as political maneuvering intensifies ahead of the 2027 election.

events.headline: MK Party Polls at 55% in eThekwini Ahead of South Africa's November Municipal Elections
events.summary: A new poll shows the MK Party commanding 55% support in the eThekwini (Durban) metro area ahead of South Africa's November 4 municipal elections, far outpacing the ANC's 10%, as Jacob Zuma's party continues to gain ground in KwaZulu-Natal.

events.headline: Jamaica Receives First Flight of US Third-Country Deportees Under Bilateral Deal
events.summary: A flight carrying 22 third-country migrants deported from the US landed in Kingston on Oct 13, 2026, the first under a June 2026 bilateral memorandum of understanding. The agreement caps arrivals at 25 deportees per fortnight.

events.headline: ASML Reports Record €11.7 Billion Q3 Revenue, Warns AI Chip Demand Will Outstrip 2027-2028 Supply
events.summary: ASML reported record third-quarter 2026 net sales of about 11.7 billion euros, up 55% year-on-year, with net income near 5.0 billion euros and a gross margin of 57.5%. The company forecasts fourth-quarter sales of 14.2-15.2 billion euros and warned that planned 2027-2028 equipment supply capacity will not fully meet AI-driven chip demand, with some customers now seeking orders for 2029-2030.

events.headline: Seoul's US Ambassador Calls September DMZ Blast Deliberate, Sparking Clarification Row
events.summary: South Korea's ambassador to the US, Kang Kyung-wha, told lawmakers on Oct 12, 2026, that the Sept 21 DMZ landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers was 'definitely not accidental,' aligning with a Joint Chiefs of Staff finding that North Korea deliberately planted mines south of the Military Demarcation Line. Her remarks appeared to contrast with President Lee's earlier description of the incident as an 'unfortunate accident,' prompting the embassy to issue a clarification on Oct 14.

events.headline: WHO Finds No Evidence of Ongoing Plague Transmission in Irkutsk, Russia
events.summary: The World Health Organization said it found no evidence of ongoing transmission after investigating a suspected plague case in Irkutsk, Russia, easing earlier concerns about a possible outbreak.

events.headline: Indonesia Nominates Health Minister Budi Gunadi Sadikin for WHO Director-General
events.summary: Indonesia has officially nominated Health Minister Budi Gunadi Sadikin as a candidate for the next Director-General of the World Health Organization.

events.headline: Hong Kong Customs Seizes 320,000 Suspected Unmanifested Pharmaceutical Products Worth HK$18 Million
events.summary: On Oct 13, 2026, Hong Kong customs officers intercepted a lorry at the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge that had been declared to carry supplements, skincare and clothing but was found to contain about 320,000 suspected unmanifested pharmaceutical products worth roughly HK$18 million. A 39-year-old mainland Chinese male driver was arrested.

events.headline: CGIL General Strike Disrupts Trains, Buses and Waste Collection Across Tuscany
events.summary: A CGIL-called regional general strike across Tuscany on Oct 14, 2026, from 09:00 to 17:00 disrupted Trenitalia and Italo rail services, Autolinee Toscane buses, and Alia waste collection, though schools and air transport were excluded. The strike opposes Italy's 'Security Packages' legislation and shows solidarity with people facing legal proceedings over an October 2025 protest at Massa Carrara station.
